REWARD_MACHINE:
STATES: u0, u1, u2
INITIAL_STATE: u0
FINAL_STATES: u2
TRANSITION_FUNCTION:
(u0, at_exit & holding_box) -> u2
(u0, box_fell) -> u1
(u0, else) -> u0
(u1, holding_box) -> u0
(u1, else) -> u1
(u2, else) -> u2
REWARD_FUNCTION:
(u0, at_exit & holding_box, u2) -> 1.0
(u0, box_fell, u1) -> 0.25
(u1, holding_box, u0) -> 0.5
feedback: Multiple issues. 1) Task logic: u1 (hands empty after a fall) transitions back to u0 on `holding_box` — but this reward is only given once; a second fall would be a regression from u0 to u1 again with another +0.25/+0.5 cycle, making the reward unbounded and exploitable (drop/re-pick loops farm reward; progress rewards must be dense but bounded). Regressions should be explicit and one-shot if intended, but here cycling is unbounded. 2) The 'very next move' requirement is not enforced: from u1 the agent could move around for many steps before picking up; the RM gives +0.5 whenever `holding_box` becomes true, no matter how late — no deadline or decay, so 'next move pick it up' is not represented. Also nothing distinguishes immediate vs delayed pickup. 3) Terminal condition: reward only fires on `at_exit & holding_box` from u0, but the machine never verifies `siren`-related aspects — acceptable since task doesn't require siren silence; however `at_exit` with the box NOT held pays nothing and there is no explicit terminal/accepting semantics: u2 is reached only via success; reaching exit without the box leaves u0 with no reward — this is actually correct behavior, but u2 declared FINAL is only reachable through the good exit, fine. 4) Dense progress: between start and exit the machine only rewards fall/pickup; the exit itself is a sparse 1.0 — acceptable density-wise but the +0.25/+0.5 shaping gives net +0.75 for a fall/pickup cycle even if the agent later exits empty-handed? No — exit empty-handed pays 0 but the agent keeps +0.75, which is reward hacking: an agent that intentionally drops/re-picks to farm the fall cycle could exceed the optimal reward. Ensure shaped rewards can never exceed what a correct trajectory earns, e.g. deduct or gate. 5) Missing coverage: in state u0, `at_exit` alone (without holding_box) is caught by else self-loop — fine; but if the episode ends at exit with box, the machine transitions to u2, which is fine. 6) Check exact format: missing explicit `(u2, else) -> u2` exists; reward for self-loops in u1/u2 omitted — if per-state else rewards are expected, add `(u1, else, u1) -> 0.0` etc. Overall: unbounded shaping cycle and no enforcement of the 'immediately pick up again' requirement make this unsuitable as-is.

REWARD_FUNCTION:
(u0, box_fell, u1) -> -0.1
(u1, holding_box, u3) -> 0.2
(u1, at_exit & holding_box, u4) -> 1.0

feedback: Format is correct: nonempty FINAL_STATES header with u4 declared in STATES, all transition labels are predicate-only conjunctions, and every state has an else self-loop covering irrelevant propositions (siren_ringing, switch_toggled, and non-progress steps). Semantic fidelity to the task 'Should the box fall, make your very next move the one that picks it back up. If you get to the exit, you must have the box in your hands.': u0 handles the pre-fall phase (holding or not); u1 is the fallen state; the only edges out of u1 other than the else self-loop are holding_box -> u3 and the terminal at_exit & holding_box -> u4, so acceptance requires the box to be back in the hands after a fall, and a single pickup suffices. If the box fell while held, u2 -> u1 captures it. The RM accepts at_exit & holding_box which matches 'must have the box in your hands at the exit'; note that no-fall episodes reach u2 via holding_box before at_exit can fire, and the conjunction with at_exit fires on the terminating step so precedence conflicts are resolved correctly (at_exit & holding_box checked before bare box_fell/holding_box, consistent with box_fell and at_exit never co-occurring). Rewards: terminal rewards 1.0, fall penalty -0.1, re-pickup reward 0.2 — dense progress shaping with bounded magnitude; no reward is assigned on the else self-loops, so irrelevant steps are not sparsely rewarded. No regression (no transition back to earlier states) is needed by this task. Reachability holds: u1 reachable via box_fell from u0 or u2, u3 reachable via pickup after fall, u4 reachable from u0, u2, u3. Accepting state u4 self-loops absorbing. One minor note: the (u0, holding_box) -> u2 edge gives no reward and u2 is functionally identical to u0 except for the fall edge — but since box_fell -> u1 carries the penalty in both u0 and u2, this is harmless and keeps the structure compact.
